items.title: Boehringer bets big on China, offering $7B biobucks for Sino cancer programs
items.snippet: Boehringer Ingelheim is building up its China strategy, inking a deal to develop new cancer treatments with Sino Biopharmaceutical just weeks after opening an R&D facility in Shanghai.

items.title: Ultragenyx’s pivot to a smaller R&D footprint claims 20% of workforce
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: AbbVie bets up to $1.47B for Nxera’s discarded IBD program
items.snippet: AbbVie’s $100 million upfront cash payment will purchase global rights to Nxera’s deprioritized oral small molecule, which has already completed Phase 1 testing.

items.title: Amgen starts MariTide autoinjector study as pivotal readouts approach
items.snippet: With the first Phase 3 data expected for Amgen’s MariTide next year, analysts are looking for evidence that the GLP-1 candidate is tolerable. Meanwhile, the company has begun testing an autoinjector formulation.

items.title: Sanofi’s axing of Nurix STAT6 program ‘not a target-related issue’
items.snippet: Sanofi has discontinued an early-stage STAT6 degrader program licensed from Nurix Therapeutics, a decision analysts say is related to the asset itself or Sanofi’s strategic reprioritization rather than the drug class more broadly.

items.title: With MFN now embedded in pharma, execs see little impact from Democrats’ blue wave
items.snippet: Speaking on third quarter earnings calls this week, Novo and Pfizer’s CEOs see little change to their Most Favored Nation drug pricing deals, which were signed with the Trump administration last year.

items.title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
items.snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

items.title: Novo, Lilly battle for oral GLP-1 dominance with data tit for tat
items.snippet: Novo CEO Mike Maziar Doustdar insists that his company is ahead of fierce rival Eli Lilly as oral Wegovy rises to 8 million total prescriptions since its January launch.

items.title: Pfizer eyes Europe first for Lyme vaccine as prevalence rises in US
items.snippet: Since Pfizer already owns a tick-borne encephalitis franchise in Europe, the region is a natural first step for the pharma’s upcoming Lyme disease vaccine.

items.title: Q3 earnings roll on, FDA pushes rare disease, uniQure’s Huntington’s therapy reaches review
items.snippet: The majority of the large pharmas have now reported third quarter earnings—spoiler alert: Eli Lilly made more money than anyone expected. Plus, the FDA dropped another initiative aimed at accelerating rare disease treatments; HHS greenlights the compounding of six unapproved peptides; and uniQure’s embattled gene ther...

items.title: How a Ms. Frizzle-esque librarian helped Flagship’s Louisa Helms find biotech
items.snippet: BioSpace 40 Under 40 honoree Louisa Helms is a lot of things—athlete, scientist, entrepreneur and likely future biotech executive. Just don’t ask her to pick up any pipettes.

items.title: 6 potential blockbusters that could pave China’s path to 2030 ambitions
items.snippet: In its latest five-year plan, China has set its sights on developing five drugs that could each rake in more than $1 billion globally by 2030. Experts say it's well on its way, with two medications having already met that bar.

items.title: Pfizer, fresh to China’s obesity market, looks to Viagra model to compete
items.snippet: Pfizer is calling upon lessons learned from one of the first drugs ever made available on the internet—Viagra—as it commercializes a new obesity drug in China.

items.title: Compass to submit psilocybin depression drug for approval imminently after stock wobbles
items.snippet: Compass Pathways revealed that an FDA filing for COMP360 will be complete “in the next two weeks,” with an expected drug launch in the first half of next year. The update follows a reported regulatory submission for Usona Institute’s own psilocybin candidate for depression on Monday.

items.title: Lonza agrees to buy 5 Merck KGaA facilities to accelerate US expansion
items.snippet: The Swiss contract development and manufacturing organization will more than double its U.S. footprint by acquiring the Merck KGaA plants.

items.title: Neurocrine defends Prader-Willi drug after another patient death
items.snippet: Neurocrine Biosciences will conduct a new study for the rare disease drug Vykat to explore dosing and safety in patients with Prader-Willi syndrome who have complex health issues.

items.title: Novartis puts $772M BioArctic deal on ice, skates away from brain-delivery alliance
items.snippet: Novartis is discontinuing a neurodegeneration alliance with BioArctic in which the companies aimed to develop a drug candidate that could cross the blood-brain barrier.

items.title: Pfizer flat in Q3 despite 32% growth for new and acquired products
items.snippet: Sales of assets from Seagen and Biohaven grew in the third quarter, but it wasn’t enough for Pfizer to overcome declines across the Prevnar and COVID franchises.

items.title: Karyopharm files for bankruptcy, looks to merger with Ayrmid for life raft
items.snippet: Debtor-in-process financing up to $55 million could keep the lights on at Karyopharm Therapeutics for its multiple myeloma and myelofibrosis programs as the biotech waits to see if its union with Ayrmid will go through.

items.title: FDA peptide policy risks undermining drug development and patient safety
items.snippet: By allowing compounding pharmacies to produce certain unapproved peptides, the Department of Health and Human Services could, in the short term, put patients in harm’s way. Longer term, the policy shift threatens the industry that brings new medicines to market.

items.title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
items.snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
